evidence.note: Records first run's score (0.169), wall-clock (0.1 min) and iterations (15.6M) — explicit calibration of time-vs-score cost from a cheap probe.
Uses repeated 1-minute test runs to sweep nc/s3 weights and estimate convergence before committing to longer runs.
Deliberately sizes runs by difficulty: 5-min yeast, 10-min DM-HS, and explicitly reasons about probability of hitting S3=0.32 within 10 min for the larger 7k-node network.
Splits budget across both pairs by running them concurrently in background, and later parallelizes 8 SA processes for 600s to fully use cores.
Budget mismanagement: CPU contention from too many concurrent SANA processes forces a kill; prematurely killed a ~7-min DM-HS run then felt time-pressed and considered shortening.
Notes his optimizer scripts 'only write the alignment files at the end' — a checkpointing gap that risks losing work if killed mid-run.
Eventually banks best solutions: SIGINTs SANA to extract output and copies best greedy alignments to the target files before wrap-up.

reasoning: The agent deliberately used cheap 1-minute probes to estimate convergence and time cost, then sized full runs (5/10 min) according to each deliverable's difficulty and gap, and parallelized across cores — matching anchor 8 and reaching toward 10. It falls short of 10 because of genuine budget-management lapses: CPU contention forcing kills, a prematurely-killed run leaving it time-pressed, and optimizer scripts with no intermediate checkpointing (best solution only recovered at the end via SIGINT). This places it solidly at 8.
